name: crosstalk
summary: agents exchange durable messages and start coworkers across providers and paired computers.
where: Inside a claude or codex agent session, use the carnivore MCP crosstalk tools.
how_to: Send with crosstalk_send and approve first contact in the owner inbox.
Read your own messages with crosstalk_inbox or crosstalk_thread; use crosstalk_reply to respond.

Use agent_spawn with a task to start a coworker in the current folder, or choose a project or working directory. Give peer to start it on a paired computer. The new session appears as a tab beside its parent.
examples: A Claude agent asks a Codex agent to inspect a bug, and the Codex reply returns in the same thread.
A message to a busy Codex pane joins its active turn; a Claude native SendMessage appears in the same message history.
A native message absorbed by a busy Claude turn is acknowledged after its linked peer queue records show consumption.
A Claude agent spawns a Codex coworker on a requested model to fix a test; the parent receives its completion reply.
A fresh Codex coworker receives its queued task on its attached thread without a manual warmup prompt.
A configured transparent Codex YOLO launch uses native crosstalk and honors the requested model.
native messages keep their reply id while session-row identity remains separate from the provider conversation
A local agent messages a paired computer's Claude pane; the remote native inbox receives it and a reply returns through the same thread.
fork into a worktree with a child contact pinned to its durable session identity
Local fork lineage refuses a remote-host row even when its socket, pane name and epoch match.
Owner-only provider forks and prompt history are explicitly refused by the peer route inventory.
An agent asks agents_lookup for a sleeping teammate (status asleep) and crosstalk_send wakes it, once the owner approves, and delivers the question.
media_exempt: Spawn uses the existing terminal tab strip and generic phone toast; it adds no unique visual component to capture.
